subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should this IPv6-only gateway-crash report stay as a distinct guarded-fetch bug, or should maintainers explicitly fold it into the broader SSRF address-family tracker at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87763?
rationale: The likely fix touches the shared SSRF DNS-pinning dispatcher, so automation should not choose between socket-level containment, family-selection policy, and canonical issue routing without maintainer security-boundary intent.

options.title: Keep Distinct Crash Bug
options.body: Keep this issue open to require a focused regression proving IPv6-only fetch failures reject without process exit while preserving SSRF pinning.

options.title: Fold Into Address-Family Tracker
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87763 the canonical owner only if maintainers agree its fix scope includes IPv6-only process-exit containment.

options.title: Close After Live Non-Repro
options.body: Close only after current main is live-tested on an IPv6-unroutable host with IPv6-only DNS and shown to reject cleanly without gateway exit.

recommendation.title: Keep Distinct Crash Bug
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open to require a focused regression proving IPv6-only fetch failures reject without process exit while preserving SSRF pinning.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent high-confidence history signal across the shared SSRF and guarded-fetch paths.
